name: Claude
tagline: Long-form drafting and analysis that holds its thread across a whole document.
summary: Claude is a general-purpose AI assistant from Anthropic used for long-form writing, document analysis, summarisation and reasoning over large amounts of text. It handles code, structured extraction and multi-step reasoning alongside prose, which makes it a common default for drafting, editing and thinking work.

name: Grammarly
tagline: Grammar, clarity and tone corrections applied wherever you already write.
summary: Grammarly checks spelling, grammar, clarity and tone as you type, across the browser, desktop apps and documents. Its generative features rewrite sentences for concision or a target tone, so it sits at the polishing end of a writing workflow rather than the drafting end.

name: Writesonic
tagline: Blog and ad drafts generated from a brief, with SEO guidance built in.
summary: Writesonic generates marketing and blog content from a short brief, with templates for landing pages, ads and product descriptions. It bundles SEO guidance into the drafting step, which suits teams producing a high volume of search-facing content.

name: Notion AI
tagline: Writing, summarising and search that sit on top of your own workspace.
summary: Notion AI works inside a Notion workspace, drafting and rewriting page content, summarising long documents and answering questions across connected pages. Because it is grounded in the workspace it is most useful for internal documentation, specs and meeting notes rather than published prose.

name: Sudowrite
tagline: A drafting environment built specifically for fiction and narrative writing.
summary: Sudowrite is aimed at novelists and narrative writers, with features for expanding scenes, describing settings and holding character and plot notes alongside the manuscript. It is a writing environment rather than a general chat assistant.

name: QuillBot
tagline: Paraphrasing, summarising and citation help for academic and study writing.
summary: QuillBot rewrites text in a chosen register, summarises long passages and generates citations. It is used heavily in coursework and academic writing, where the task is usually restating or condensing an existing source rather than generating something new.

name: Wordtune
tagline: Sentence-level rewriting that offers several ways to say the same thing.
summary: Wordtune suggests alternative phrasings for a selected sentence, adjusting length and formality, and can summarise long documents. It targets the revision pass rather than the blank page.

name: Cursor
tagline: An AI code editor that reads the repository before it edits across files.
summary: Cursor is a code editor built around AI assistance, with codebase-aware chat, multi-file edits and inline completion. Because it indexes the whole project it is used for refactors and feature work that touch several files rather than single-line completion.

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: Inline completion and chat wired into the editors developers already use.
summary: GitHub Copilot suggests code as you type and answers questions about the current file or repository from inside the editor and on GitHub itself. Its reach across editors and its pull-request features make it the most widely deployed coding assistant.

name: Claude Code
tagline: An agentic coding assistant that works from the terminal on a real repository.
summary: Claude Code runs in the terminal and operates on a project directly: reading files, making edits, running commands and following a multi-step task through to a diff. It suits larger changes and refactors where the work spans many files and several steps.

name: Windsurf
tagline: An AI-first editor with an agent that carries a task across the codebase.
summary: Windsurf is an editor with an integrated agent that plans and applies changes across a project, alongside conventional completion and chat. It also ships editor plugins for teams that do not want to switch IDE.

name: Replit
tagline: Prompt to a running application inside a hosted development workspace.
summary: Replit is a browser-based development environment with an AI agent that scaffolds, edits and deploys applications without local setup. The hosting and the editor being in one place makes it a common route for a first working prototype.

name: Tabnine
tagline: Code completion with self-hosted and privacy-controlled deployment options.
summary: Tabnine provides completion and chat across many languages and editors, with deployment options that keep code inside a customer environment. That control is its distinguishing feature for teams with strict code-handling requirements.

name: v0
tagline: Generates React and Tailwind interfaces from a prompt or a screenshot.
summary: v0 turns a description or a reference image into working React components styled with Tailwind, which can be copied into a project or iterated on in the browser. It sits between design and implementation: the output is code, not a mockup.

name: Vercel AI SDK
tagline: An open-source toolkit for building AI features into TypeScript applications.
summary: The Vercel AI SDK is a TypeScript library for calling language models, streaming responses and wiring tool calls into web applications, with one interface across providers. It is developer infrastructure rather than an end-user product.

name: Postman
tagline: API design, testing and documentation with AI assistance across the workflow.
summary: Postman is an API development platform for sending requests, organising collections, writing tests and publishing documentation. Its AI features help generate tests, documentation and request setups from an existing API definition.

name: Figma
tagline: Collaborative interface design with AI assistance for drafting and editing.
summary: Figma is the standard collaborative interface design tool, covering layout, components, prototyping and developer handoff in one file. Its AI features generate first-draft layouts and help rename, rewrite and rearrange existing designs.

name: Canva
tagline: Template-driven design for social, decks and print with generative tools built in.
summary: Canva is a browser design tool built on templates, aimed at people who are not full-time designers. Its Magic Studio features generate images, edit photos, resize designs for different channels and draft presentations.

name: Framer
tagline: Design and publish a real website from one canvas, with AI-assisted layout.
summary: Framer combines a design canvas with a publishing pipeline, so a site is designed and shipped from the same file. Its AI features generate page layouts and copy from a prompt and translate a design into responsive breakpoints.

name: Uizard
tagline: Turns rough sketches and text prompts into editable wireframes and screens.
summary: Uizard generates multi-screen app and web mockups from a text description, a screenshot or a hand-drawn sketch, and keeps the result editable as design components. It targets the earliest, roughest stage of interface work.

name: Recraft
tagline: Generates vector artwork, icons and brand assets in a consistent style.
summary: Recraft generates illustrations, icons and mockups as editable vectors rather than raster images, and can hold a defined style across a set of assets. That style consistency is what makes it usable for a brand system rather than one-off images.

name: Looka
tagline: Generates logos and a matching brand kit from a name and a few preferences.
summary: Looka produces logo options from a business name, industry and style choices, then extends the chosen mark into a brand kit of colours, fonts and templated assets. It covers the specific moment where a new venture needs an identity quickly.

name: Gamma
tagline: Turns an outline into a formatted presentation, document or web page.
summary: Gamma generates presentations, documents and simple sites from a prompt or an outline, applying layout and theming automatically. It removes the slide-by-slide formatting work that usually dominates deck building.

name: Beautiful.ai
tagline: Presentation software where slides re-layout themselves as content changes.
summary: Beautiful.ai builds decks from smart templates that adjust their layout automatically when content is added or removed, and can generate a first draft deck from a prompt. It is aimed at business presentations that must stay on-brand.

name: Midjourney
tagline: Stylised image generation with unusually strong art direction.
summary: Midjourney generates images from text prompts and reference images, with a distinctive aesthetic and fine control over style. It is used where the look of the image matters more than literal accuracy.

name: Ideogram
tagline: Image generation that reliably renders legible text inside the picture.
summary: Ideogram generates images from prompts with a particular strength in rendering readable typography, which most image models handle poorly. That makes it practical for posters, logos-in-context and social graphics that carry words.

name: Adobe Firefly
tagline: Generative image and editing models wired into the Adobe toolchain.
summary: Adobe Firefly generates and edits images, including generative fill and expansion, and is available both standalone and inside Photoshop and Illustrator. Its integration with existing Adobe files is the main reason design teams reach for it.

name: Photoroom
tagline: Removes and replaces photo backgrounds, with batch editing for product shots.
summary: Photoroom cuts subjects out of photographs, replaces backgrounds and generates product scenes, including in bulk. It is built around ecommerce and marketplace imagery, where the same operation is applied to hundreds of shots.

name: Leonardo.Ai
tagline: Image generation with reusable trained styles and fine-grained controls.
summary: Leonardo.Ai generates images with control over composition and style, and lets users train and reuse custom style models. It is used where a set of images has to stay visually consistent across a project.

name: Descript
tagline: Edit video and audio by editing the transcript, as if it were a document.
summary: Descript transcribes a recording and lets you cut the video by deleting words in the transcript, along with filler-word removal, screen recording, captions and voice cleanup. Editing long interview and podcast footage is dramatically faster this way than on a conventional timeline.

name: Opus Clip
tagline: Turns one long recording into ranked short-form clips, captioned and reframed.
summary: Opus Clip takes a long video or podcast, finds the segments most likely to work as short-form content, reframes them vertically and adds captions. It exists specifically to make repurposing long footage into shorts fast.

name: Runway
tagline: Generative video, inpainting and cleanup tools in a single timeline.
summary: Runway generates video from text and images and provides editing tools such as object removal, background replacement and motion controls. It is used both for generated footage and for cleanup work on real footage.

name: CapCut
tagline: Short-form video editing with auto-captions, effects and templates.
summary: CapCut is a video editor for short-form social content, with automatic captions, background removal, templates and effects on both desktop and mobile. It is the default editor for a large share of vertical video.

name: Kling
tagline: Text and image to video generation with steady motion across longer shots.
summary: Kling generates video clips from text prompts or a starting image, with controls for camera motion and shot length. It is used for generated sequences rather than for editing existing footage.

name: Synthesia
tagline: Presenter-led videos generated from a script using AI avatars and voices.
summary: Synthesia turns a written script into a video presented by an AI avatar, in many languages, without a camera or studio. It is used for training, product explainers and internal communication where filming is impractical.

name: HeyGen
tagline: Avatar video generation plus translation and lip-sync for existing footage.
summary: HeyGen generates avatar-presented video from a script and can translate an existing video into another language with matched lip movement. It covers both making new presenter video and extending the reach of video that already exists.

name: VEED
tagline: Browser video editing focused on subtitles, cleanup and social formats.
summary: VEED is a browser-based video editor with automatic subtitles, translation, background noise removal and resizing for social platforms. It is aimed at fast turnaround rather than complex timelines.

name: ElevenLabs
tagline: Speech synthesis and voice cloning that hold up across long scripts.
summary: ElevenLabs generates speech from text in many languages and can clone a voice from a sample, with controls for delivery and pacing. It is widely used for narration, dubbing and voiceover where recording is impractical.

name: Suno
tagline: Generates complete music tracks, including vocals, from a written brief.
summary: Suno produces full songs from a text description of genre, mood and lyrics, including instrumentation and vocals. It is used for background music and scratch tracks where licensing real music is a barrier.

name: Adobe Podcast
tagline: Cleans up recorded speech to sound as if it were recorded in a studio.
summary: Adobe Podcast enhances recorded speech by reducing background noise and reverb, and provides browser-based recording and editing for spoken audio. It targets the specific problem of usable audio recorded in a bad room.

name: Otter.ai
tagline: Live meeting transcription with searchable notes and summaries.
summary: Otter.ai joins meetings, transcribes them in real time and produces summaries and action items that stay searchable afterwards. Its value is in the record it leaves behind rather than in the transcription itself.

name: Murf
tagline: Studio-style voiceover production with timing and background tracks.
summary: Murf generates voiceover from a script with a library of voices, and provides a timeline for syncing narration to slides or video and layering background audio. It is oriented toward finished voiceover deliverables rather than raw speech synthesis.

name: Perplexity
tagline: Answers questions from live sources and shows the citations behind them.
summary: Perplexity answers questions by searching the web and citing the pages it drew from, and keeps follow-up questions on the same thread. The citations are the point: it is used where an answer has to be checkable.

name: Elicit
tagline: Screens academic papers and extracts findings into a comparable table.
summary: Elicit searches academic literature, screens papers against criteria and extracts specified fields from each one into a table. It automates the mechanical part of a literature review rather than the judgement.

name: NotebookLM
tagline: Answers questions strictly from the sources you upload, with inline citations.
summary: NotebookLM grounds its answers in a set of documents the user provides, citing the passage behind each claim, and can produce summaries and audio overviews of that material. Because it will not answer outside the sources, it suits close reading of a fixed corpus.

name: Consensus
tagline: Searches scientific papers and summarises what the evidence actually says.
summary: Consensus searches peer-reviewed literature for a specific question and summarises the direction and strength of the findings across papers. It is aimed at answering empirical questions rather than browsing a field.

name: ResearchRabbit
tagline: Maps how papers cite each other so a literature can be explored visually.
summary: ResearchRabbit builds a visual graph of related papers and authors from a starting set, surfacing work a keyword search would miss. It is a discovery tool for the shape of a field.

name: SciSpace
tagline: Reads a paper alongside you and explains passages, maths and terminology.
summary: SciSpace answers questions about an uploaded paper, explains equations and jargon in place, and can compare several papers side by side. It targets the moment of actually reading a difficult paper.

name: Surfer SEO
tagline: Content briefs and on-page scoring measured against the current ranking set.
summary: Surfer SEO analyses the pages currently ranking for a keyword and produces a brief with structure and term guidance, then scores a draft against it. It connects writing decisions to what is already winning the search result.

name: Buffer
tagline: Schedules social posts across channels and drafts variations for each one.
summary: Buffer queues and publishes social content across networks, with an assistant that repurposes a post for different platforms and suggests ideas. Its role in a workflow is the distribution step.

name: Copy.ai
tagline: Campaign copy and outbound sequences generated from a single brief.
summary: Copy.ai generates marketing copy and multi-step go-to-market sequences from a brief, and can run those as repeatable workflows across a list. It targets volume copy production rather than a single considered piece.

name: Jasper
tagline: Brand-tuned marketing content produced at team scale with shared voice rules.
summary: Jasper generates marketing content against a stored brand voice and style guide so output stays consistent across a team, with campaign-level workflows. The brand controls are what distinguish it from a general assistant.

name: Clay
tagline: Enriches lead lists from many data sources and drafts the first outreach.
summary: Clay builds and enriches prospect lists by combining many data providers in a spreadsheet-like interface, then uses that data to personalise outbound messages. It is the research-and-targeting half of outbound, not the sending.

name: AdCreative.ai
tagline: Generates ad creatives and headline variants scored for likely performance.
summary: AdCreative.ai produces sets of ad images and headline variations sized for each platform and ranks them by predicted engagement. It is built around producing many variants for testing rather than one hero asset.

name: Julius AI
tagline: Analyses an uploaded dataset from plain-English questions and returns charts.
summary: Julius AI takes a spreadsheet or CSV and answers questions about it by writing and running analysis code, returning charts and explanations. It covers exploratory analysis for people who do not want to write the code themselves.

name: Hex
tagline: Collaborative data notebooks with SQL, Python and AI-assisted analysis.
summary: Hex is a notebook environment where SQL and Python cells can be published as interactive apps, with AI assistance for writing queries and explaining results. It is aimed at analytics teams sharing work with stakeholders.

name: Rows
tagline: A spreadsheet with live data connectors and AI functions in the formula bar.
summary: Rows is a spreadsheet that pulls live data from external services and exposes AI operations as ordinary formulas for classifying, extracting or summarising cell contents. It suits recurring reports assembled from several sources.

name: Deepnote
tagline: A collaborative Python notebook with an AI assistant for analysis steps.
summary: Deepnote is a hosted notebook for Python and SQL with real-time collaboration and an assistant that drafts and fixes analysis code. It is the shared workspace end of data work rather than the dashboard end.

name: ChatGPT
tagline: A general assistant with browsing, file handling and custom instructions.
summary: ChatGPT is a general-purpose assistant that handles writing, analysis, code and image generation, with web browsing, file uploads and reusable custom instructions. Its breadth makes it a common first stop before a specialised tool.

name: Gemini
tagline: A general assistant wired into Google documents, mail and long-context reading.
summary: Gemini is a general assistant available standalone and inside Google Workspace, where it can draft in documents, summarise mail and work across long files. The Workspace integration is what distinguishes it for people already in those tools.

name: Zapier
tagline: Connects thousands of apps into triggered automations without code.
summary: Zapier links applications so an event in one triggers actions in others, with AI steps that classify, extract or draft along the way and agents that carry out multi-step tasks. Its breadth of integrations is its defining feature.

name: Relay.app
tagline: Multi-step automations that pause for human approval at the risky steps.
summary: Relay.app builds automations across apps with AI steps, and lets a run wait for a person to review or edit before it continues. That human-in-the-loop step is what makes it usable for work with consequences.

name: Make
tagline: Visual automation builder for branching, multi-step workflows across apps.
summary: Make lays automations out on a visual canvas, supporting branching, iteration and error handling across many connected services, with AI modules available as steps. It handles more complex logic than a linear trigger-action tool.

name: n8n
tagline: Source-available workflow automation that can be self-hosted and extended in code.
summary: n8n builds automations on a node canvas and can run on your own infrastructure, with the option to drop into JavaScript for any step and build AI agent workflows. It suits teams that need automation to stay inside their own environment.

name: Glean
tagline: Searches and answers across every internal system a company already uses.
summary: Glean indexes a company documents, tickets, chats and wikis and answers questions from them with citations, respecting existing permissions. It addresses the problem of knowledge that exists but cannot be found.

name: Fathom
tagline: Records and summarises meetings, then pushes the follow-ups into the CRM.
summary: Fathom joins calls, records and transcribes them, and produces summaries and action items that sync into CRM and task tools. It closes the loop between a conversation and what happens afterwards.

name: GitHub
tagline: Where code lives — its official MCP server lets an agent open PRs and manage issues directly.
summary: GitHub hosts code, pull requests and issues. Its official MCP server lets an AI agent read repositories, open pull requests, manage issues and search code on a developer's behalf, instead of a person relaying each step by hand.

name: Slack
tagline: Team chat an agent can search, post to and automate through its official MCP server.
summary: Slack is where teams talk. Its official MCP server lets an AI agent search channel history, post updates and trigger workflows on a team's behalf, instead of a person copying context between the two.
